requirement:
During report conversion, on a terminal enabled under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.processes.progress.terminal`, Habeas MUST
display updating progress with elapsed time and completed and total
test-attempt counts. The total MUST count the recorded attempts selected for
conversion. An attempt MUST advance the completed count only after its
conversion has finished or reported a collection failure, including processing
its associated child-process profiles. These counts MUST measure conversion
work regardless of the attempt's test outcome.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation of `requirements.test-coverage.processes.progress`.

- **Updating display with elapsed time and completed/total counts.**
  - `src/execution_coverage/progress.rs#mod[tests]/fn[stage_and_conversion_counts_are_visible_then_cleared]` builds a conversion `Progress` with totals 0 and 2. It calls `completed()` and asserts that the bar position and the drawn text show `{n}/{total} attempts` and a `[00:00:` elapsed field. It also asserts the display is monochrome and clears on drop.
  - `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[coverage_progress_on_a_pty_preserves_reports_and_plain_output_policy]` runs the real binary on a PTY with `TERM=xterm`. It asserts `Converting coverage`, `1/1 attempts`, `[00:` and in-place escape sequences. `NO_COLOR` is set, and the test asserts no color codes appear.
- **Total counts the recorded attempts selected for conversion.**
  - In the implementation, `fn[finish]` passes `attempts.len()` to `Progress::conversion`. This is a pass-through with no conditional.
  - The unit test checks displayed totals of 0 and 2. The PTY test checks `1/1` against exactly one recorded attempt, and it asserts the saved run has one record.
- **Advance only after conversion has finished, including child-process profiles.**
  - `src/execution_coverage/runner.rs#mod[tests]/fn[parallel_conversion_is_bounded_and_retains_every_result_in_order]` asserts in the completion callback that the work for that item has already finished. It runs with 2 and 8 workers over twice as many items. It also asserts every item is visited once and results keep their order.
  - The PTY `test(child_process)` case has two profiles per attempt. It asserts a `1/1 attempts` display that is cleared, and it asserts both child-process profiles are retained.
- **Counts measure work regardless of test outcome, and collection failures also complete.**
  - The runner test makes one item return `Err`. It asserts `completed == total`, so failed work still advances the count.
  - The PTY test runs a failing test (`deliberate_failure`, outcome `failed`) and a test whose profile is missing (`missing_profile`, which gives a collection diagnostic). It checks the cleared `1/1 attempts` conversion display in both cases.
- **Terminal gating and clearing.** These obligations sit in the cited `processes.progress.terminal` requirement, so they only need to be applied in this case. The tests apply them:
  - The PTY test runs `dumb` and a redirected stderr. Neither emits the conversion display or escape sequences.
  - The unit test asserts the display clears for empty (total 0) and completed conversions.

I found no plausible violating behavior that these tests would accept.

text: During report conversion, on a terminal enabled under
display updating progress with elapsed time and completed and total
test-attempt counts. The total MUST count the recorded attempts selected for
conversion. An attempt MUST advance the completed count only after its
conversion has finished or reported a collection failure, including processing
its associated child-process profiles. These counts MUST measure conversion
work regardless of the attempt's test outcome.
Habeas coverage progress MUST be displayed when stderr is an interactive
terminal and `TERM` is not `dumb`. `NO_COLOR` MUST disable color without
disabling progress. When stderr is redirected or `TERM=dumb`, Habeas coverage
progress MUST NOT emit animation or terminal control sequences.
Temporary progress displays MUST be cleared when their stage ends, including
empty work and early collection failures. Final diagnostics and the coverage
artifact location MUST remain readable. Progress reporting MUST NOT change
coverage results, retained profiles, or command exit status.
